result.text:
Halberg Textiles GmbH is carrying strained and poorly documented exposure with its insurer Adlerhof Trade Credit (CL01). Six invoices are open, the worst of them INV000220 at €55,300 and 40 days past due, and total open exposure of ~€527,100 sits against a €440,000 credit limit — the buyer is already over the granted limit. There is no settled payment history at all, so the trend is recorded as "insufficient_history" and no behavioural pattern can be assessed; the credit limit was last reviewed in Nov 2024 and may be stale against current exposure. Alongside this, a Metro Business Daily report of 2025-10-20 describes the Bielefeld unit moving from three shifts to one on weak order inflow, with contract workers not recalled and material procurement slowing; the company confirmed only a "temporary realignment of production".

The score is 42.7, placing the buyer in the Watch band (35-60) and away from the 60 High Risk threshold, with a PD of 0.3267. The trace is 0.65 x 60.0 (payment, 40 DPD) + 0.35 x 10.5 (news) = 42.7, so the payment leg contributes a weighted 39.0 and the news leg only 3.7 — a severity 3 capacity-cut story decayed from a base of 20.0 to 10.49 over 340 days. The adjudicator agreed with caveats: the band is defensible on the formula's inputs, but the score is driven entirely by days-past-due and is blind to both the over-limit position across 6 open invoices and the absence of any settlement track record behind the 60.0 payment raw. The reviewer also flagged that the article's publication date and the 2026-08-16 payment evidence date do not reconcile with the 340 age_days used for decay — the effect is small and over-decays rather than inflates — and that the capacity-cut account rests on two anonymous sources and a former employee. Treat 42.7 as a Watch reading with an exposure caveat rather than a comfortable mid-band one.

The recommendation for Adlerhof Trade Credit (LIM0006) is FREEZE: current limit €440,000, revised limit €440,000, change 0, on the grounds that the buyer is already owed at or above the limit so there is nothing left to cut. Expected loss is unchanged at 116436 before and after, and the maximum liability constraint does not bind. The practical action is to stop new cover and work the over-limit balance down rather than to reprice the line.

Relief depends on the payment file, not the news. Settlement of the 40-days-past-due invoice INV000220 and reduction of the ~€527,100 open balance back under the €440,000 limit would remove the over-limit position and lower the payment leg that supplies the weighted 39.0. A run of settled invoices would replace the "insufficient_history" trend flag with a real payment pattern, giving the 60.0 payment raw a track record behind it, and a fresh review of the limit last set in Nov 2024 would align cover with actual exposure. On the news side the severity 3 item is already heavily decayed and contributes only 3.7, so confirmation that the Bielefeld single-shift move is the temporary realignment the company describes — rather than a step toward escalation — would keep that leg immaterial. Against a PD of 0.3267 versus a target of 0.25, sustained on-time settlement is the route back.
